title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as the Space Force continues to invest heavily in satellite capabilities, while startups scramble to navigate the defense landscape. Meanwhile, international developments and technological advancements hint at a rapidly evolving strategic environment.

themes.title: Space Force's Big Bet
themes.body: The Space Force's $4.16 billion award to SpaceX for airborne target tracking satellites underscores a pivotal shift towards reliance on commercial partnerships. This move not only boosts SpaceX's already impressive portfolio but also signals the military's increasing trust in private sector innovation.

themes.title: Startups Eye Defense Market
themes.body: With the Space Force's commercial gatekeeper offering guidance, defense startups are eager to tap into government contracts. The playbook may help demystify the often opaque world of defense procurement, but the competition will remain fierce.

themes.title: China's Rocket Ambitions
themes.body: China's imminent launches of new reusable rockets highlight its determination to expand its presence in space. As geopolitical tensions simmer, these advancements may shift the balance of power in orbital capabilities.

themes.title: Funding Flows in Space Tech
themes.body: True Anomaly's recent $190 million Series C round illustrates the growing investor appetite for space technology firms. As defense needs evolve, capital is increasingly directed towards companies that can offer innovative solutions in this critical sector.
